lessons.title: Nutritional Requirements by Age and Purpose
lessons.body: Ducks need different nutrients at different stages: starter (0-2 weeks), grower (3-8 weeks), finisher (9 weeks to market), and layer (for egg production). Starter feed should have 20-22% protein, 0.9% calcium, and 0.4% available phosphorus. A good starter mash in Africa can be made from maize meal, soybean meal, fishmeal, and a vitamin-mineral premix. For example, mix 55% maize, 25% soybean meal, 10% fishmeal, 8% wheat bran, and 2% premix. This gives about 21% protein. Grower feed: 16-18% protein, 0.8% calcium. Finisher: 14-16% protein, 0.8% calcium. Layer feed: 16-18% protein, 3.5-4% calcium for strong eggshells. If you keep ducks for meat, focus on energy and protein for rapid growth. For eggs, calcium and protein are critical. Local ingredients like cassava, sweet potato, and moringa can replace some maize and soybean, but adjust to avoid nutrient gaps. Always provide clean waterâducks drink up to 1 liter per day per adult. Without proper nutrition, ducks grow slowly, lay fewer eggs, and get sick easily. Weigh your ducks weekly: a healthy Pekin should reach 2.5-3 kg in 8-10 weeks. If they are underweight, increase protein and energy. Use a simple kitchen scale or a hanging scale for accuracy. In Africa, many farmers use commercial feeds from companies like Vital, Ugachick, or local millers. If you mix your own, use a feed formulation table or ask an extension officer. Never guessâwrong ratios waste money and harm birds. Adjust feed as seasons change: in cold weather, ducks need more energy; in hot weather, they eat less, so increase nutrient density. Always store feed in dry, cool place to prevent mold.

lessons.title: Commercial Feed Types and Formulations
lessons.body: Commercial duck feeds come as mash, pellets, or crumbles. In Africa, common brands include Vital, Ugachick, Nutri, and local miller mixes. For ducks, choose feeds labeled for ducks or poultry with similar protein levels. Starter crumbles (0-2 weeks) are easy for ducklings to eat. Grower pellets (3-8 weeks) reduce waste. Finisher pellets (9+ weeks) for meat. Layer mash or pellets for egg-laying ducks. If you cannot find duck-specific feed, use chicken feed but adjust: ducks need more niacin (vitamin B3). Add 10-15 mg niacin per kg of feed, or supplement with brewer's yeast. A typical commercial formulation: Starter: 20% protein, 2,900 kcal ME/kg. Grower: 17% protein, 3,000 kcal ME/kg. Finisher: 15% protein, 3,100 kcal ME/kg. Layer: 17% protein, 3.5% calcium, 2,800 kcal ME/kg. If you mix your own, use a digital scale for accuracy. A simple 100 kg batch of grower feed: 50 kg maize, 20 kg soybean meal, 10 kg fishmeal, 10 kg wheat bran, 5 kg limestone, 3 kg bone meal, 1 kg salt, 1 kg premix. Mix thoroughly on a clean concrete floor or in a drum mixer. Store in airtight bags away from moisture. Commercial feeds are convenient but costly. Many African farmers blend commercial feed with local ingredients to cut costs. For example, replace 20% of commercial feed with chopped greens or kitchen waste, but ensure the total protein remains adequate. Always check expiration dates and avoid moldy feed. Mold produces aflatoxins that can kill ducks. If feed smells musty or has clumps, discard it. Buy from reputable suppliers and ask for a feed analysis certificate. For small flocks, buy small quantities to avoid spoilage. For large flocks, order in bulk and store in a dry, ventilated room on pallets. Never feed ducks moldy or wet feed.

lessons.title: Supplementary Feeding with Greens and Insects
lessons.body: Ducks love greens and insects, and these can cut feed costs by 20-30% while improving health. Safe greens include: amaranth leaves, sweet potato vines, cabbage, kale, spinach, water hyacinth (chopped), duckweed, and azolla. Duckweed is a superfood for ducksâit contains 25-35% protein and grows in ponds. You can grow duckweed in a shallow pit with animal manure. Harvest daily and feed fresh. Azolla is another aquatic fern with 20-25% protein. Insects: termites, black soldier fly larvae (BSFL), earthworms, and crickets. BSFL are excellentâthey contain 40-45% protein and 30% fat. You can breed BSFL in a bin with kitchen waste. Termites can be trapped using a plastic container filled with dry grass and a little water, buried upside down. Ducks will eat them eagerly. Feed greens and insects as supplements, not main diet. For growing ducks, give 50-100 g of greens per duck per day, and 20-50 g of insects. For layers, give 100-150 g greens and 30-60 g insects. Chop greens finely to prevent choking. Never feed moldy, wilted, or sprayed greens. Avoid toxic plants like cassava leaves (raw), tomato leaves, and potato leaves. Introduce new feeds gradually over 5-7 days to avoid digestive upset. Ducks also eat snails, slugs, and small fishâthese are good protein sources. In Africa, many farmers let ducks scavenge in rice paddies, gardens, and ponds. This reduces feed costs but can expose ducks to predators and diseases. If you free-range, provide supplemental feed twice a day. A simple supplement mix: 1 part chopped greens, 1 part cooked cassava, 1 part insects, mixed with a little commercial feed. This gives balanced nutrition. Always provide clean water for drinking and foraging. Ducks need water to swallowânever feed dry feed without water. Greens and insects also provide water. Monitor ducks' weight and egg production; if they drop, increase commercial feed.

lessons.title: Feeding Schedules and Ration Calculation
lessons.body: Ducks need a consistent feeding schedule. Feed adults twice a day: morning (7-8 am) and evening (4-5 pm). Ducklings (0-2 weeks) need feed available all dayâuse shallow feeders. From 3 weeks, feed three times a day. Layers: feed twice a day, but provide calcium (oyster shell) free-choice. Meat ducks: feed twice a day, but restrict to avoid overfat. A simple rule: ducks eat about 100-150 g of feed per day for growing, 150-200 g for layers. But calculate based on body weight and purpose. For meat ducks, feed 3-4% of body weight daily. For layers, 150 g per day plus greens. To calculate ration: Determine total feed needed per day = number of ducks Ã daily feed per duck. For 10 growing ducks at 120 g each = 1.2 kg per day. For 10 layers at 160 g = 1.6 kg per day. Mix your feed in a wheelbarrow or basin. Use a weighing scaleâkitchen scale for small amounts, hanging scale for large. If you don't have a scale, use a known container: a 1-liter cup holds about 500 g of feed. But weighing is more accurate. Feed in clean, shallow troughs or trays. Ducks are messyâthey will spill and waste feed. Use feeders with lips to reduce waste. Never let feed sit in feeders for more than a few hours, especially in humid climatesâit gets moldy. Remove leftover feed and clean feeders daily. Provide water in deep containers so ducks can dip their heads and clean their nostrils. Ducks need water to swallow. Always have water available. Adjust feed based on season: in hot weather, feed early morning and late evening when it's cool. In cold weather, feed more energy-rich feeds like maize. Monitor feed consumptionâif ducks suddenly eat less, they may be sick. Keep records: date, number of ducks, feed type, amount, and notes. This helps you track costs and productivity. For 100 layers, you need about 16 kg feed per day. At $0.50 per kg, that's $8 per day. Plan your budget accordingly.

lessons.title: Waterfowl-Specific Feed Supplements
lessons.body: Ducks have specific nutritional needs that differ from chickens. The most critical is niacin (vitamin B3). Ducklings fed chicken feed without added niacin can develop leg deformities, weak legs, and difficulty walking. Add niacin at 10-15 mg per kg of feed, or supplement with brewer's yeast (1-2% of feed). If you see ducklings with bowed legs, add niacin immediately. Another key nutrient is vitamin E and selenium for immune function and fertility. Add 20-30 IU vitamin E and 0.1 mg selenium per kg feed. Calcium and phosphorus must be balanced: for layers, 3.5-4% calcium, 0.4% available phosphorus. For growers, 0.8% calcium, 0.4% phosphorus. Too much calcium for growing ducks causes kidney damage. Use limestone or oyster shell for calcium, and bone meal or dicalcium phosphate for phosphorus. Ducks also need omega-3 fatty acids for egg quality and health. Add 1-2% fish oil or flaxseed oil to layer feed. In Africa, you can use local sources: moringa leaves (rich in vitamins), papaya leaves, and pumpkin seeds. Moringa leaf meal can replace 5-10% of feed and provides vitamins A, E, and K. Pumpkin seeds are a natural dewormer and provide zinc. For waterfowl, provide grit (small stones) to help digest food. Ducks that free-range pick up grit naturally. For confined ducks, offer a bowl of grit (crushed granite) free-choice. Also provide oyster shell free-choice for layers. Salt: add 0.3-0.5% salt to feed, but never moreâexcess salt causes poisoning. A simple supplement mix for 100 kg feed: 100 g niacin, 50 g vitamin E, 50 g selenium premix, 500 g brewer's yeast, 1 kg moringa leaf meal, 500 g pumpkin seed meal. Mix thoroughly. Always follow label instructions for commercial premixes. Overdosing vitamins can be toxic. Store supplements in cool, dark place. If you use commercial duck feed, it usually has these supplements already. But if you mix your own, you must add them. Check with an extension officer or vet for specific recommendations for your region.

lessons.title: Avoiding Common Feeding Mistakes
lessons.body: Many duck farmers lose money and birds due to avoidable feeding mistakes. The most common: feeding moldy feed. Mold produces aflatoxins that cause liver damage, poor growth, and death. Always smell feed before givingâif musty, discard. Store feed in dry, cool place on pallets, not on floor. Another mistake: not providing enough water. Ducks need water to swallow and digest. Without water, they choke and die. Provide deep water containers (at least 10 cm deep) so ducks can submerge their heads. Change water daily. Third: feeding only maize or kitchen scraps. This causes protein and vitamin deficiencies. Ducks need balanced feed with protein, energy, vitamins, and minerals. Fourth: overfeeding layers. Fat ducks lay fewer eggs. Restrict feed to 150-160 g per day for layers. Fifth: not adjusting feed for age. Feeding starter to adults wastes money; feeding layer feed to ducklings causes kidney damage from excess calcium. Sixth: sudden feed changes. Always transition over 5-7 days by mixing old and new feed. Seventh: using chicken feed without niacin. Ducklings need extra niacin. Eighth: feeding toxic plants: raw cassava leaves, tomato leaves, potato leaves, and avocado leaves. These contain toxins that can kill ducks. Ninth: not providing grit. Ducks need grit to grind food in their gizzard. Tenth: feeding on dirty ground. Ducks pick up feces and bacteria. Use clean feeders and trays. Eleventh: not weighing feed. Guessing leads to under- or overfeeding. Use a scale. Twelfth: ignoring weight loss or drop in egg production. These are signs of illness or poor feed. Act quickly. Thirteenth: feeding too much salt. Salt poisoning causes thirst, diarrhea, and death. Keep salt at 0.3-0.5% of feed. Fourteenth: not storing feed properly. Rats, mice, and insects contaminate feed. Use airtight containers. Fifteenth: feeding expired commercial feed. Vitamins degrade over time. Check dates. By avoiding these mistakes, you will save money and have healthier ducks. Keep records and observe your birds daily. If something seems wrong, consult a vet or experienced farmer.

quiz.q: What is the recommended protein level for duck starter feed (0-2 weeks)?
quiz.explanation: Starter feed needs 20-22% protein for rapid growth and development.

quiz.q: Which nutrient is especially critical for ducklings to prevent leg deformities?
quiz.explanation: Ducklings require extra niacin; deficiency causes weak legs and bowed legs.

quiz.q: How much calcium should layer duck feed contain?
quiz.explanation: Layers need 3.5-4% calcium for strong eggshells.

quiz.q: What is a good local protein source for ducks in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Duckweed contains 25-35% protein and is safe and easy to grow.

quiz.q: How much feed does a growing duck typically eat per day?
quiz.explanation: Growing ducks consume about 100-150 g of feed daily.

quiz.q: What is the main danger of feeding moldy feed to ducks?
quiz.explanation: Mold produces aflatoxins that damage the liver and can be fatal.

quiz.q: Why should you not feed layer feed to ducklings?
options: C) Excess calcium can damage kidneys
D) It has too much niacin
quiz.explanation: Layer feed has high calcium which can cause kidney damage in growing ducks.

quiz.q: What is a safe way to transition ducks to a new feed?
options: B) Mix old and new over 5-7 days
quiz.explanation: Gradual transition over 5-7 days prevents digestive upset.

quiz.q: Which of these is a toxic plant for ducks?
quiz.explanation: Raw cassava leaves contain cyanide and are toxic to ducks.

quiz.q: How much water does an adult duck drink per day?
quiz.explanation: Adult ducks drink about 1 liter of water daily.

quiz.q: What is the protein content of black soldier fly larvae?
quiz.explanation: BSFL are high in protein (40-45%) and fat, excellent for ducks.

quiz.q: What is a simple way to provide niacin to ducklings?
quiz.explanation: Brewer's yeast is rich in niacin and can be added at 1-2% of feed.

quiz.q: How often should you feed adult ducks?
quiz.explanation: Adult ducks are typically fed twice daily, morning and evening.

quiz.q: What is the recommended salt level in duck feed?
quiz.explanation: Salt should be 0.3-0.5% of feed; excess causes poisoning.

quiz.q: Which supplement helps with egg quality and provides omega-3?
quiz.explanation: Fish oil or flaxseed oil provides omega-3 fatty acids for better eggs.

quiz.q: Why do ducks need grit?
options: B) To help digest food in the gizzard
quiz.explanation: Grit helps grind food in the gizzard, aiding digestion.

quiz.q: What is a sign of niacin deficiency in ducklings?
quiz.explanation: Niacin deficiency causes bowed legs and difficulty walking.

quiz.q: How much greens can you feed to a growing duck per day?
quiz.explanation: Growing ducks can be given 50-100 g of chopped greens daily as supplement.

quiz.q: What is the danger of feeding too much calcium to growing ducks?
quiz.explanation: Excess calcium can cause kidney damage in growing ducks.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good way to store feed?
options: B) In airtight containers on pallets
quiz.explanation: Airtight containers on pallets protect feed from moisture and pests.

quiz.q: What is the protein level for duck grower feed?
quiz.explanation: Grower feed should have 16-18% protein for steady growth.

quiz.q: How can you tell if commercial feed is spoiled?
quiz.explanation: Musty smell indicates mold; such feed should be discarded.

quiz.q: What is a cheap local source of vitamins for ducks?
quiz.explanation: Moringa leaves are rich in vitamins A, E, and K and can be added to feed.

quiz.q: What is the daily feed amount for a layer duck?
quiz.explanation: Layers need about 150-160 g of feed per day.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid feeding ducks on dirty ground?
options: B) They pick up feces and bacteria
D) They get too much grit
quiz.explanation: Feeding on dirty ground exposes ducks to harmful bacteria and parasites.

quiz.q: What is a sign that ducks are not getting enough feed?
quiz.explanation: A drop in egg production or weight loss indicates inadequate nutrition.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of using pellets over mash?
quiz.explanation: Pellets reduce spillage and waste compared to mash.

quiz.q: How much niacin should be added per kg of duck feed if mixing your own?
quiz.explanation: Add 10-15 mg niacin per kg of feed for ducklings.

quiz.q: What is a safe way to feed kitchen scraps to ducks?
options: B) Chop and mix with feed
quiz.explanation: Chop scraps and mix with balanced feed to avoid nutritional gaps.

quiz.q: What is the main reason to keep records of feed consumption?
options: B) To track costs and productivity
quiz.explanation: Records help monitor costs, feed efficiency, and bird health.
